read.where: Rum is distilled from **sugarcane**: its juice, its syrup or **molasses** (what’s left after making sugar). There is no single world rulebook; each country sets its own rules. In the EU, rum is bottled at **37.5% or more**.

keyPoints.line: is made from fresh cane juice.
has its own appellation for it.

read.bigIdea: Fresh cane juice tastes grassy and bright.
read.where: Most rum is made from molasses. **Rhum agricole** is made from **fresh cane juice**, which tastes grassy and bright. In the EU the “agricultural” term is only for rum from the **French overseas departments** and **Madeira**; **Martinique** has its own appellation for it. **Cachaça**, from **Brazil**, is also made from cane juice: it’s the spirit in a **Caipirinha**.

keyPoints.line: rum is light: unaged or filtered.
rum is richer: longer aging or caramel.

read.where: **White** rum is unaged or filtered after aging, so it’s light. **Gold** has some time in wood. **Dark** rum is richer, from longer aging or added caramel. **Spiced** rum is flavored with spices like vanilla and cinnamon. Rum from **pot stills** tends to be heavier; from **column stills**, lighter.

keyPoints.line: is rum, lime, orange curaçao and orgeat.
is rum with Campari and pineapple.

read.where: The **Daiquiri** is rum, lime and sugar. The **Mojito** adds mint and soda. The **Mai Tai** is rum, lime, orange curaçao and orgeat. The **Dark ’n’ Stormy** is dark rum and ginger beer. The **Piña Colada** is rum, pineapple and coconut. The **Jungle Bird** brings in Campari.
